strata.definition: {expt}|S{stage}|A{drug_addition}; contrasts only within a stratum against its own vehicle arm

tiers.t1: TIER 1 - STRONG: total>=11, no zero on reproducibility/LODO/coherence/specificity/confounder
tiers.t2: TIER 2 - PROMISING: total>=7, at most one zero among reproducibility/LODO/coherence/confounder

warnings.text: CHEM11 (three 48 hpf strata, 7 drugs each) is the primary discovery regime. All axes and loadings shown are fit there.

CHEM10 is a technical-distribution-shift test (different fixative, strain, 2.3x depth), not a clean biological generalization set. Only the neural axis transfers (loading r=+0.90); mesenchymal +0.02; module 3 -0.30.

The neural program is strongly driven by LY411575 / Notch inhibition (LODO 0.275; pooled CHEM10 transfer falls to 0.33 without it). It is NOT yet proven Notch-independent. Named for its genes, not the drug.

Module 3 (hindbrain + muscle + retina) is anatomically incoherent, internally contradictory in enrichment, and transfers negatively. Scores Tier 2 only because the pre-registered rubric is permissive; treat as provisional.
The organism-wide shared axis (removed before all axes here) is generic and carries zero drug identity (discrimination 0.000). The uncorrected version was a DMSO/EtOH vehicle artifact.

Drug-specific residual interpretation is more reliable for some drugs than their dense direction: Cyclopamine, DEAB and SU5402 show canonical targets down in 3/3 strata while their full residual direction does not reproduce (dense 0.03-0.13).
All responses are corrected for the EtOH-vs-DMSO placebo axis measured within each stratum. Six drugs are DMSO-referenced; Cyclopamine is EtOH-referenced.
V0: an intuition-building tool over frozen Phase 3-5 results, not a polished demo. Every value traces to DATA_MAP.md.
